paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in Paul's goodbye. He doesn't sail past these elders with a wave. He calls them in, because he wants them ready for what comes after he's gone. And look at what he can say about his time with them: "I did not shrink back from declaring to you the whole will of God." (Acts 20:27) He gave them all of it, not just the easy parts.

Then he hands them the job. "Keep watch over yourselves and the entire flock," he says, and "Be shepherds of the church of God." (Acts 20:28) He warns them that savage wolves will come, and that even from their own number, men will rise up and distort the truth (Acts 20:29-30). So the church is worth guarding, and the guarding starts with knowing the real thing well enough to spot a fake. That's why you're in the Word, baker. It's how you keep your footing when someone sounds sure but isn't telling the truth.

And notice what Paul leaves them holding, friend: "And now I commit you to God and to the word of His grace, which can build you up…" (Acts 20:32) He won't be there, but the Word will be, and so will God, and I think a good shepherd stays close to both. He also reminds them what Jesus said: "It is more blessed to give than to receive." (Acts 20:35) Paul's road isn't finished yet, and neither is this story.
